Then C* <= K* <= C* + min(2/ln 2, C*) and C* - 3/ln 2 <= K*_lambda <= C*. Pointwise for nonconstant g: min_i D_i/d_i <= H/I + min(2/ln 2, H/I) and min_i lambda_i/d_i <= (sum_i B_i)/I <= H/I. Equivalently, FEI holds iff there is an absolute K such that every f has a coordinate i with KL(nu_i||q_i) >= log2(1/Inf_i(f)) - K.

pending.exact_statement: For every complete tree and every coordinate rule, E sum_t (D_t - C d_t) = H(f) - C I(f); for a stopping tree it equals (H(f)-C I(f)) - E[H(g_tau) - C I(g_tau)]. The minimal nonnegative potential Q*_v = max(0, D_v - C d_v + avg Q*_children) (Q*=0 at leaves) satisfies D_t <= C d_t + Q_t - E[Q_{t+1}|F_t], is dominated by every nonnegative potential with that property, and gives H(f) <= C I(f) + Q*_root; Q*_root = 0 under the greedy D/d rule whenever C >= K*. Hence positive expected whole-path debt on a complete tree is exactly a counterexample to H <= C I, independent of the rule, and stopping-rule falsifiers can only target Q*.

pending.exact_statement: Let f be a Boolean sign on a finite uniform cube whose nonzero Fourier support lies in c+V, dim_F2 V<=d. If e_i is not in V then B_i(f)=H(S_i|S_-i)=0. If every relevant i has e_i in V then f depends on at most d coordinates. The class of such f (support condition imposed per disjoint factor) is closed under coordinate restriction and disjoint products, and B_i, Inf_i are factor-local. Hence if every nonconstant Boolean function of at most d variables has a relevant i with B_i<=K Inf_i, every nonconstant member of the class has one, and H(f)<=(K+2/ln 2)I(f) for every member (C005 erasure induction).
